title: Tiered KV reservoir: prefetch throttling, paged frames and OOM graceful degradation
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: As models get longer and more concurrent sessions hit a single GPU host, our KV cache must balance memory residency with latency SLOs. Current paged/blocked implementations cause tail latency spikes and occasional GPU OOMs under pathological access patterns (dense token reuse + many cold sessions).

Goal: Implement a tiered KV reservoir that separates small hot frames, bulk paged frames, and transient hitchhiker frames with coordinated prefetch throttling and graceful OOM fallback. The design should: 1) improve steady-state token latency by keeping hot frames resident, 2) reduce premature prefetching during high oversubscription, 3) provide deterministic backpressure and fallbacks when GPU memory is constrained, and 4) be observable and tunable from the Console.

Scope and approach:
- Introduce three frame tiers: HOT (resident, low eviction priority), WARM (candidate for async prefetch), and COLD (paged, high eviction priority).
- Reservoir accounting: maintain per-host watermarks (soft/high) and per-model affinity budgets so one noisy model cannot evict hot frames for other tenants.
- Prefetch throttling: a token-bucket style controller that gates the number of concurrent async prefetches based on recent GPU residency churn and in-flight generation latency.
- Blocked/paged eviction policy: evictions operate at page granularity using blocked allocations (contiguous KV slices) to avoid fragmenting L2/L3 buffers; coalesce adjacent freed pages and prefer evicting COLD then WARM frames.
- OOM mitigation: on high-pressure events, immediately stall new prefetches, accelerate compaction of WARM->COLD, and trigger graceful model fallback (lower capacity variant or host spill routing) before catastrophic OOM.
- Telemetry and rollout: add metrics for tier occupancy, prefetch throttle tokens, prefetch latency, eviction rate, and OOM triggers. Implement a canary rollout with synthetic load and a simulator harness before fleet rollout.

Implementation notes:
- Core changes in runtime: reservoir accounting module, prefetch controller, and a blocked page allocator with coalescing.
- Compatibility: keep ABI compatible with existing kernel scheduler; expose knobs via config (max_hot_frames_per_model, prefetch_rate_limit, soft/high watermarks).
- Performance testing: run generator workload with mixed sequence lengths and cold-start spike bursts. Key SLAs: 95p token latency delta < 10% vs baseline under typical load, and 99.9p OOM events reduced to zero in synthetic stress tests.
